text.aria-label: Title text 'Figure 18: WeatherNext 3's error against ENS mean-vector reference for the three wind farms, in the months before July, from July, and pooled'
text.tspan: Figure 18: WeatherNext 3's error against ENS mean-vector reference for
the three wind farms, in the months before July, from July, and pooled

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Each mark is an XGBoost model's error, given one forecast product, in percent of capacity, or the difference between two such models in points of capacity. Top panel: WeatherNext 3's error minus the reference's, on the same rows. Lower panels: each product's own error. Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months. Filled dots are WeatherNext 3; hollow diamonds are the reference. A hollow black square with a dashed line, just right of a dot, is the same quantity at the sensitivity XGBoost setting. The three colours are three groups of the same out-of-fold rows: February to June 2026 (4 calendar months), July to September 2026 (3 months), and every row from February to September 2026 (7 months). Only the second group is certain to lie after WeatherNext 3's training data, so it checks whether a change of model version at the start of July shows in the scores; the third group, which mixes both, is the leaderboards' WeatherNext 3 row. The second group's intervals resample only 3 months, fewer than the 6 that support an interval, so they show the range of the months and are indicative only. Each calendar month occurs in one year only, so every contrast is descriptive. Every product is scored on exactly the same hours. Every error is a fraction of the generator's own capacity, taken as its 99th percentile of metered output.'
text.tspan: Each mark is an XGBoost model's error, given one forecast product, in percent of capacity, or the difference
between two such models in points of capacity. Top panel: WeatherNext 3's error minus the reference's, on the same
rows. Lower panels: each product's own error. Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months.
Filled dots are WeatherNext 3; hollow diamonds are the reference. A hollow black square with a dashed line, just
right of a dot, is the same quantity at the sensitivity XGBoost setting.
The three colours are three groups of the same out-of-fold rows: February to June 2026 (4 calendar months), July to
September 2026 (3 months), and every row from February to September 2026 (7 months). Only the second group is
certain to lie after WeatherNext 3's training data, so it checks whether a change of model version at the start of
July shows in the scores; the third group, which mixes both, is the leaderboards' WeatherNext 3 row. The second
group's intervals resample only 3 months, fewer than the 6 that support an interval, so they show the range of the
months and are indicative only. Each calendar month occurs in one year only, so every contrast is descriptive.
Every product is scored on exactly the same hours. Every error is a fraction of the generator's own capacity, taken
as its 99th percentile of metered output.
